content:
Mathlib has a general definition docs#IsCompl of complementary objects in a partial order: being disjoint (inf = bot) and codisjoint (sup = top). This applies to the submodules of a module but has a tiny disadvantage over semirings: this does not imply that the ambient module is isomorphic to the product of the two submodules, a condition which is clearly useful but strictly stronger. As a consequence, several functions (such as docs#Submodule.projectionOnto) are restricted to rings, just because they can't use the probably more appropriate Submodule.IsCompl.

This is not that I believe that modules over semirings are absolutely fundemental, but this makes the linear algebra library a bit uneven in some places.
Do we have an application where it's important?
Important, certainly not, but in #37745, every of these little but technical trivialities would have worked for semirings, and we are forced to pass to docs#Ring.
For me, it's mainly a matter of coherence. I'm ready to do linear algebra in semirings whenever the math works (in the same way), but if mathlib blocks it, I'll probably stop.
